holidays.name: National Best Friends Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the people who know your worst stories and stick around anyway. Celebrate with a phone call, a surprise snack delivery, or a long overdue hangout with your ride-or-die.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of greeting-card and social media culture in the United States. It is often listed on June 8, although a separate Best Friends Day is also marked on other dates.
holidays.funFact: Researchers who study friendship say it can take around 200 hours of time together to turn someone into a close friend.

holidays.name: National Jelly-Filled Doughnut Day
holidays.description: A sweet salute to the doughnut that fights back with a surprise gush of fruity filling. Bite carefully unless you want jam on your shirt.
holidays.origin: Doughnut-themed food days are a staple of the American food holiday calendar, and this one is observed on June 8 in several lists of food observances.
holidays.funFact: Jelly doughnuts are a long-running Hanukkah tradition in Israel, where they are called sufganiyot.

holidays.name: World Oceans Day
holidays.description: A day for honoring the big salty thing that covers most of the planet. People celebrate with beach cleanups, documentaries, and by promising to use fewer plastic straws.
holidays.origin: Proposed in 1992 at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, it was officially recognized by the United Nations in 2008 and has been celebrated every June 8 since.
holidays.funFact: The ocean produces roughly half of the oxygen we breathe, so every other breath you take is basically thanks to the sea.

holidays.name: Name Your Poison Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for choosing your favorite vice, whether that is coffee, chocolate, or binge-watching TV. It is about owning your guilty pleasures with a wink.
holidays.origin: This is a lighthearted unofficial observance from online holiday calendars with no single known founder, tied to the idea of picking your preferred indulgence.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'name your poison' dates back to at least the 1800s as a way to invite someone to pick a drink.

holidays.name: Upsy Daisy Day
holidays.description: A cheerful observance meant to help you get out of bed on the right side and tackle the day with a smile. Think of it as a permission slip to be annoyingly positive before noon.
holidays.origin: A whimsical unofficial holiday inspired by the old British expression 'upsy-daisy', which people say when helping a child up after a tumble.
holidays.funFact: Upsy-daisy comes from the 1700s word 'up-a-daisy' and was originally used when lifting babies into the air.
